title: Canonicalize OpenFX as the mandatory provider-neutral VFX plug-in interoperability standard profile
decisions: OpenFX 1.5.1 is the pinned standards reference for image-effect plug-in interoperability; it is not an architectural authority or a mandatory runtime implementation.
Every OpenFX execution declares and negotiates the required API version and suites; missing capabilities fail closed without silent downgrade.
Natron remains the existing optional, replaceable, non-authoritative open-source reference host and is not duplicated.
Natron RB-2.6 documents OFX 1.4 host support, so it cannot attest OpenFX 1.5-only suites without separate executable evidence.
OpenFX plug-ins are native code and require allowlisted immutable digests, dependency and license inventory, SBOM, malware/behavioral scanning and signature or exception evidence before loading.
Governed rendering executes in a dedicated constrained worker with network deny by default, staged output, crash containment and no direct mutation of canonical editorial state.
Accelerator selection is capability-discovered through the existing Host Resource Broker; stable UUID and PCI BDF identify the lease, while runtime ordinals remain ephemeral.
Requested and observed execution backends must match; silent CPU, accelerator, display-GPU or cloud fallback is forbidden.
Input, working and output color spaces plus OCIO configuration identity are explicit and carried into render provenance.
Reference CI PASS proves contract and fail-closed policy behavior only; current-host production promotion requires a real admitted host/plugin render, QC, GPU/color/provenance and rollback evidence.
